answer.sourceLine: These are Anne Frank’s own words, written in her diary on Tuesday, 7 March 1944 and printed in the 1952 English translation of ‘The Diary of a Young Girl’ by B. M. Mooyaart-Doubleday. The famous short line is a genuine excerpt of that translation; later English editions word the same Dutch sentence a little differently.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: The Diary of a Young Girl (Het Achterhuis)

source.excerpt: I don’t think then of all the misery, but of the beauty that still remains… Whoever is happy will make others happy too. He who has courage and faith will never perish in misery!
trail: The 1952 English translation prints the line verbatim — “Whoever is happy will make others happy too. He who has courage and faith will never perish in misery!” — attributed to The Diary of a Young Girl (1952) ↗.
The passage sits in the diary entry headed Tuesday, 7 March 1944 ↗, where Anne contrasts her mother’s outlook with her own faith in the beauty that remains.
Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗ carries the same diary line in a later translation: “A person who’s happy will make others happy; a person who has courage and faith will never die in misery!”
source.excerptNote: As rendered in the 1952 Mooyaart-Doubleday translation of the 7 March 1944 entry.

author.name: Anne Frank
author.heading: About Anne Frank
author.bio: Annelies Marie ‘Anne’ Frank (1929–1945) was a German-born Jewish girl whose diary, kept while hiding from the Nazis in an Amsterdam annex from 1942 to 1944, became one of the most widely read books in the world. She died in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp in early 1945; her father Otto, the family’s only survivor, had the diary published in Dutch in 1947. The 7 March 1944 entry is among her most quoted, written as she reflected on finding beauty and happiness despite her circumstances.

misattribution.heading: The catch
misattribution.intro: Anne Frank really did write this — but two things trip people up.

items.why: The familiar ‘Whoever is happy will make others happy too’ is the 1952 Mooyaart-Doubleday translation. The 1995 Definitive Edition (translated by Susan Massotty) renders the same Dutch sentence as ‘A person who’s happy will make others happy’ (Wikiquote) ↗, so a reader checking a modern paperback may not find the exact popular phrasing.

Anne Frank is one of the internet’s biggest magnets for fabricated feel-good quotes, so skepticism is healthy. Unlike many circulating lines, this one is traceable to a real diary entry — the 7 March 1944 passage ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: Authentic Anne Frank — her diary entry of 7 March 1944, quoted here from the 1952 English translation ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Anne wrote the line during her second year in hiding, in an entry that pushes back against her mother’s counsel to cope with misery by contemplating the suffering of others. Anne’s answer was the opposite: go outside, look at the sun and nature, and ‘think of all the beauty in yourself and in everything around you and be happy.’
The sentence about happiness spreading to others is the hinge of that argument — happiness, for Anne, is not private but contagious, and the source of resilience even ‘in misfortune.’
